Tiny Little Office

What leaves your browser

Tiny Little Office keeps a document in its link. Opening one asks the site for its own files and nothing else. This page lists every other request the site can make: when it happens, what it carries, and what stops it. The Content-Security-Policy in public/_headers allows these places and no others, so a request not on this list is refused by the browser itself.

A document fetches nothing from any other site. A link in it is words that go somewhere when the reader follows them; nothing in a document is drawn from another site's address.

Why each of these is asked directly

  • The map. Map tiles only while a map is on the screen; place search only when a search is tapped. They are asked directly: OpenStreetMap's usage policies are written for the browser that shows the map asking them directly, and a cache of ours in between would be the heavy, anonymous use they ask people not to make. The site sends no referrer.
  • Short links. Only when a short link is made, opened, updated or forgotten; the service holds ciphertext it cannot read, whose key is in the short link's fragment, which browsers never send (tinier/tinier.ts).
  • Sharing to a service. Share's Bluesky, Mastodon, X and LinkedIn open that service's own compose box in a new tab, with the title and the link in it: no script of theirs runs here. The link is the document, so whoever reads the post can read it. "Any https address" there is the Mastodon server the person names.
  • Fonts and icons. Self-hosted, from the site itself; the full icon set is a chunk of the site's own, loaded when the icon picker opens.
  • Links. A link in a document that leaves the site opens only after the reader is shown where it goes and says Go (kit/link-guard.ts), in a new tab with no referrer.

Nothing else

No analytics, no error reporting, no fonts or scripts from a CDN, no tag manager, no fetch the person did not cause. test/network.test.ts reads the source (src/ and the shortener in tinier/) and fails on any host that is not on this page, and on any analytics, error-reporting, font-CDN or tag-manager host anywhere in the site.

How this page is kept true

It is written from src/kit/network.ts, the one list of every host, by scripts/network-doc.ts (npm run docs:network, which npm run build runs first); a test fails when the committed page is not what the list says. Every module that asks the web takes its host from that list, so a new host cannot be reached without appearing here. The policy's connect-src and img-src are written from the same list (scripts/headers.ts), and test/csp.test.ts holds each host to the directive the list names and nothing else; the policy has no frame-src or media-src of its own, so no frame, film or sound comes from another site.

Written from src/kit/network.ts; the same page is docs/network.md in the repository.
